answer: Private set intersection over MPC lets two organizations find common members without revealing their full lists, and the voyage of the technique is that only the intersection is learned. The ocean of the design is an oblivious pseudorandom function that blinds each element before comparison, so neither side sees the other's non-matching entries. A person trying to register twice is caught when their identifier appears in both sets, and the yarrow of the protocol keeps honest members private while duplicates are exposed.
